messages.author: James Kress
messages.body:
I am looking to find suggestions on the best application for docking
proteins to DNA.
Is AMBER alone sufficient or are other apps like npDOCK, HAADOCK, HDOCK
better suited to this task?
There is a plethora of apps one can find mentioned doing a web search.  What
would the AMBER community suggest is a best choice?
Thanks for any responses.
Jim Kress
James Kress Ph.D., President

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Wed, Jun 12, 2024, James Kress via AMBER wrote:
>I am looking to find suggestions on the best application for docking
>proteins to DNA.
>
>Is AMBER alone sufficient or are other apps like npDOCK, HAADOCK, HDOCK
>better suited to this task?
Other apps are definitely needed: Amber is not designed to do docking.  I
hope you will get some suggestions that concentrate on protein--DNA docking.
Be sure to look for application papers in this area, and see what was used.
....dac

messages.author: Andrea H. Kasun
messages.body:
I also got nice results with pyDockDNA:
https://model3dbio.csic.es/pydockdna
I suggest trying several programs and comparing the results...
Good luck!
Andrea

messages.author: Cianna Calia
messages.body:
In addition to standard docking tools like HADDOCK, you may want to check
out some fairly new tools: AlphaFold 3 and RoseTTAFold-All-Atom.
https://blog.google/technology/ai/google-deepmind-isomorphic-alphafold-3-ai-model/
https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adl2528
Best of luck,
Cianna
